s3Setup.title: Connect your S3-compatible storage
s3Setup.body: Driven talks directly to your bucket with an access key you create. Nothing passes through anyone else's servers.
s3Setup.endpointHint: The service's S3 API address. For Amazon S3 use the regional endpoint; for Cloudflare R2 use your account's S3 endpoint.
s3Setup.regionHint: Leave blank unless your provider requires a specific region.
s3Setup.prefixHint: Confines Driven to one subtree, so it can share a bucket with your other data.
s3Setup.pathStyleHint: Required by MinIO and by Cloudflare R2's account endpoint. Turn it off only if your provider needs bucket-in-hostname URLs.
s3Setup.secretKeyHint: Stored in your operating system's keychain, never in Driven's database.
s3Setup.trashWarning: S3 has no trash: when Driven removes a backed-up file it is deleted permanently. Enable bucket versioning on your provider if you want to be able to recover deletions.

localFolderSetup.title: Choose your backup folder
localFolderSetup.body: Driven copies your files straight into a folder you own - a USB drive, an external disk, a NAS share, or anywhere on this computer. There is no account to connect and nothing goes over the network.
localFolderSetup.folderHint: Pick the drive or folder Driven should back up into. Driven writes a small marker file there so it can tell your drive apart from an empty folder if it is ever disconnected.
localFolderSetup.displayNameHint: How this destination appears in Driven. Defaults to the folder's name.
localFolderSetup.trashWarning: This destination has no trash: when Driven removes a backed-up file it is deleted permanently.
localFolderSetup.removableWarning: If the drive is disconnected, Driven pauses this account and tells you to reconnect it - it will never quietly back up to the empty folder left behind.

sftpSetup.title: Connect over SSH (SFTP)
sftpSetup.body: Driven talks directly to your server over SFTP with the credentials below. Nothing passes through anyone else's servers.
sftpSetup.rootPathHint: This folder must already exist on the server - Driven never creates it for you. Create it over SSH first, then point Driven at it.
sftpSetup.privateKeyHint: Paste the PEM-encoded private key text, not a file path.
sftpSetup.passphraseHint: Leave blank if the key has no passphrase.
sftpSetup.trashWarning: This destination has no trash: when Driven removes a backed-up file it is deleted permanently.
sftpSetup.fingerprintConfirmed: Connected. Driven pinned this server's host key: {fingerprint}. Every later connection is checked against it.
sftpSetup.adoptedNote: This server already held a Driven backup at this path - Driven is reusing it, so everything already there stays reachable.

step1.title: Welcome to Driven
step1.body: Driven backs up your local folders - one way, fast, with optional encryption, scheduling, and battery awareness.

step2.title: Connect your Google account
step2.body: Driven uses your own Google OAuth credentials so your data never passes through anyone else's servers.

step2.awaitingCallback: Waiting for you to finish signing in...

guide.summary: How do I get a Client ID and secret? (about 5 minutes)
guide.intro: Driven never sees your Google password, and your files never pass through anyone else's servers. You create a free OAuth client in your own Google Cloud account and paste its ID and secret below. Here is exactly how:
guide.step1: Open the Google Cloud Console at console.cloud.google.com and sign in. Click the project menu in the top bar, click "New Project", give it a name (for example "Driven Backup"), click "Create", then select the new project.
guide.step2: In the left menu, open "APIs & Services", then "Library". Search for "Google Drive API", open it, and click "Enable".
guide.step3: Open "Google Auth Platform", then "Branding", and click "Get started". Enter an "App name", pick your address for "User support email", then click "Next".
guide.step4: For "Audience", choose "External" and click "Next". Enter your email under "Contact Information", click "Next", agree to the policy, then click "Create".
guide.step5: Open the "Audience" page. Under "Test users", click "Add users", enter your own Google email, and click "Save". Only test users can sign in until the app is published.
guide.step6: Open "Google Auth Platform", then "Clients" (or "APIs & Services" > "Credentials" > "Create credentials" > "OAuth client ID"). Click "Create client", set "Application type" to "Desktop app", then click "Create".
guide.step7: Copy the "Client ID" and "Client secret" shown in the dialog and paste them into the fields below. The secret is only shown once, so copy it now.
guide.testingCaveat: Note: while your project stays in the "Testing" publishing status, Google expires the sign-in after about 7 days, so you will occasionally have to sign in again. To make it permanent, click "Publish app" on the "Audience" page once everything works.

rules.bundleSmallFilesLabel: Bundle small files in cold folders
rules.bundleSmallFilesNote: Packs many tiny, unchanged files from the same folder into a single compressed archive before uploading, cutting round-trips and rate-limit pressure at the destination. Only old files in dense folders are bundled; new or recently-changed files still upload individually. Off by default.
rules.autoStartOnLoginLabel: Launch Driven when I sign in
rules.autoStartOnLoginNote: Starts Driven in the background at login so backups keep running. Registers as a real startup app (Windows Task Manager, macOS Login Items, Linux autostart).
rules.pauseWhenOfflineLabel: Pause backups when the internet is unreachable
rules.pauseWhenOfflineNote: Turn this off if you back up to a destination that doesn't need internet access, like a LAN server or a local folder - backups keep running even while Driven can't reach the internet.
rules.adaptiveParallelismNote: Tunes how many files upload at once based on measured throughput and disk load, starting from the concurrent-uploads value above. Turn off to hold that number fixed.

vssBanner.title: Locked files are being skipped
vssBanner.body: Some files (Outlook data files, live databases, VM disks) are held open and need Volume Shadow Copy to back up, which requires elevation. Turn on the least-privilege helper below to elevate only the snapshot (not the whole app), or right-click Driven and choose Run as administrator to include them.

rules.vssHelperLabel: Use the least-privilege helper for locked files
rules.vssHelperNote: Back up locked files (Outlook data files, live databases, VM disks) by elevating only a small snapshot helper - the app itself stays un-elevated. Turning this on prompts you for elevation once, right now.
rules.vssHelperPending: Waiting for elevation approval - approve the Windows prompt to enable locked-file backup.
rules.vssHelperDeclined: Elevation was declined, so locked files are still skipped. Turn this off and on again to retry.
rules.apfsSnapshotLabel: Back up locked files using an APFS snapshot
rules.apfsSnapshotNote: Back up files that are held open (live databases, VM disks, mail stores) by mounting a read-only APFS local snapshot - only a small helper gets administrator access, the app itself stays un-elevated. Turning this on asks for your administrator password once per app session.
rules.apfsSnapshotTccNote: This does not help with files macOS privacy protection blocks - a snapshot cannot read around a denial. Those need Full Disk Access.
rules.apfsHelperPending: Waiting for administrator approval - approve the macOS prompt to enable locked-file backup.
rules.apfsHelperDeclined: Administrator approval was declined, so locked files are still skipped. Turn this off and on again to retry.
rules.menuBarIntro: Show live backup info next to the Driven icon in the menu bar.
rules.menuBarWidthHint: More than two metrics makes the menu bar item wide.
rules.telemetryNote: Anonymous usage stats only - no file names or contents are ever sent. One click to disable.

hooks.title: Backup hooks
hooks.note: Commands run in your shell once per backup cycle. A non-zero exit from the before-hook skips that backup. DRIVEN_HOOK, DRIVEN_ACCOUNT_ID, and (for the after-hook) DRIVEN_RESULT are set.

customCa.title: Corporate root certificate
customCa.label: Custom root CA (PEM file path)
customCa.note: For corporate networks that inspect TLS traffic. Point this at a PEM file holding one or more trusted root CA certificates; Driven ADDS them to the operating system's trust store for every outbound connection - it never replaces the built-in roots or disables certificate checks. Applies to new connections after an app restart. Leave blank to trust only the system's roots.
customCa.invalid: Could not read this file as a PEM certificate bundle. Check the path and that the file contains PEM certificate(s).

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.valid: Valid - this proxy configuration is usable.
proxy.invalid: This proxy configuration is not usable. Check the URL scheme (http, https, socks5, socks5h) or that the PAC file can be reached and defines FindProxyForURL.
proxy.requiresUrl: Enter a proxy URL (manual) or PAC file location (automatic).
proxy.note: Routes ALL of Driven's outbound connections through a proxy. "Use system / environment proxy" honours the HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment variables (the default). Manual takes one proxy URL (http, https, socks5, or socks5h - the 'h' resolves DNS at the proxy). Automatic evaluates a PAC (proxy auto-config) file per destination. Applies to new connections after an app restart. A broken proxy is rejected on save rather than silently connecting directly.

schedule.label: Only back up during a schedule window
schedule.note: Outside this window backups pause and resume automatically. Times are in this computer's local time zone.

browser_open_failed.long: Driven could not open your browser for Google sign-in. Use the "Open the sign-in page" button below, or copy the link into your browser to continue.

invalid_grant.long: This account's credentials expired, were revoked, or no longer grant access. Reconnect the account to continue backing up.

consent_required.long: Google needs you to grant access. Complete the sign-in to continue.

network_unreachable.long: Driven could not reach accounts.google.com. Check your internet connection and try again.

rate_limited.long: The destination asked Driven to slow down. Driven is backing off and will retry automatically.

daily_quota_exhausted.long: The destination's daily request limit was reached. Driven will resume after the limit resets.

quota_exhausted.long: The destination is out of space. Free up space there (or upgrade the plan) to continue backing up.

upload_size_limit.long: This file exceeds the destination's maximum file size and cannot be uploaded.

checksum_mismatch.long: The uploaded file did not match its checksum. Driven will re-upload it.

unreachable.long: The destination is unreachable right now. Driven will keep retrying.

remote_file_missing.long: The backed-up copy of this file was missing at the destination; it will be re-uploaded automatically on the next scan.

resumable_session_invalid.long: A resumable upload session expired. Driven will restart the upload.

dest_folder_missing.long: The destination folder was deleted. Pick a new destination to resume backups.

dest_folder_permission_denied.long: The destination folder is no longer writable by this account. Check its permissions.

file_locked.long: A file could not be read because another program has it locked. Driven will retry later.

vss_unavailable.long: Backing up locked files needs Volume Shadow Copy, which requires running Driven elevated.

vss_helper_pending.long: The least-privilege helper is starting to back up a locked file. Driven will retry it on the next cycle.

permission_denied.long: Driven is not allowed to read this file. Grant it access to back the file up; until then Driven skips it and retries each time it runs.

file_changed_during_upload.long: A file changed while it was being uploaded. Driven re-queued it for the next cycle.

file_replaced_during_upload.long: A file was replaced while it was being uploaded. Driven re-queued it for the next cycle.

io_error.long: Driven hit a disk error reading a file. Check the drive and try again.

path_too_long.long: A file path exceeds the operating system's length limit and was skipped.

unicode_collision.long: Two files have names that normalize to the same text. Rename one to back both up.

disk_full.long: The disk ran out of space during a read or restore. Free up space and try again.

invalid_filename.long: A file has a name the destination will not accept (a reserved name or trailing dot/space) and was skipped.

ads_skipped.long: An NTFS alternate data stream was skipped; the file's main contents were backed up.

offline.long: Your device reports no network connection. Backups will resume when you are back online.

no_internet.long: You are connected to a network but the internet is unreachable.

dns_failed.long: Driven could not resolve a known-good domain. Check your DNS settings.

captive_portal.long: A captive portal is blocking access. Sign in to the network and try again.

timeout.long: A request took too long and timed out. Driven will retry.

intermittent.long: The connection is unstable. Driven paused requests and will retry shortly.

proxy_required.long: An HTTP proxy requires authentication. Update your proxy settings.

endpoint_unreachable.long: Driven could not reach the update server. Try again later.

signature_invalid.long: The update's signature could not be verified and was rejected for your safety.

manual_required_macos.long: Automatic updates are not available on macOS. Download and reinstall the latest release to update Driven.

key_missing.long: The encryption key for this source was not found in the keychain.

decrypt_failed.long: A file could not be decrypted. The data may be corrupt or the key is wrong.

recovery_phrase_invalid.long: That recovery phrase failed its checksum. Check the words and their order.

db_locked.long: Driven's database is briefly locked. This usually clears on its own.

db_corrupt.long: Driven's database failed an integrity check. Rebuilding from your backup is advised.

reconcile_orphan.long: Driven found a remote file with no local record and reconciled it during startup.

no_version_as_of.long: One or more selected files have no backed-up version from before the selected date. Choose a later date, or clear the date to restore the latest backup.

timeout.long: A stress-test scenario exceeded its time budget.

bug.long: Driven hit an unexpected error. Please export a diagnostic bundle and report it.

invalid_input.long: One of the values you entered is not valid. Check the highlighted field and try again.

root_missing.long: That path does not exist on the server. Driven never creates it for you - create the folder over SSH first, or fix the path, then try again.
